scope: New 16.3B gate against the canonical master-order 16.3B flow and checks, and its use of the 16.3A factory.

findings.summary: First draft: a handed-off order skipped the requirements check, and a completion or handoff timestamp before acceptance was not refused.
findings.reproduced: Found by reading the draft before the first run.
findings.fix: Handoff now requires complete requirements (HANDOFF_BEFORE_QUALITY_GATE); handoff and completion times must not precede acceptance.
regression: negative controls: handoff before requirements accepted, records before acceptance accepted

findings.summary: A complete order whose deadline passed got OWNER_REVIEW_REQUIRED with no manifest, so a late handoff the owner chose could not be bound to exact files.
findings.reproduced: Frozen held-out H05 and primary P43 failed on the first run (16.3B_PRE_REPAIR_FOCUSED.json).
findings.fix: A missed deadline still returns the gated manifest when requirements and every deliverable pass; status stays OWNER_REVIEW_REQUIRED. The test helper's intermediate expectation for a late handoff changed from HANDOFF_READY to OWNER_REVIEW_REQUIRED; H05's scenario and final assertion are unchanged.
regression: negative controls: late complete order loses its manifest, late manifest despite open requirements

findings.summary: Paid or unknown production cost was checked only for the current revision round, so spend in an earlier round could disappear from view.
findings.fix: Every recorded artifact's cost class is checked.

observationsNotDefects: The plan step of the canonical flow is the 16.3A measured delivery scenario re-derived at acceptance; its work minutes drive AT_RISK.
AT_RISK is conservative: the full planned work minutes are compared with the time left while any deliverable is short.
Receipts identify bytes by digest; the gate does not read files. Byte checks belong to the caller that collects receipts.
